item.content: {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=methods+for+autonomous+problem+discovery+in+open-ended+intelligent+agents&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists.\", \"abstract\": \"Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level \\\"Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy.\\\" We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.\", \"doi\": \"10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0\", \"pmid\": \"42864384\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13658227\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Autonomous Chemistry and Materials Innovation Driven by Scientific Agents.\", \"abstract\": \"Large language model (LLM)-based agents are reshaping how self-driving laboratories (SDLs) may support autonomous chemical and materials research. Although SDLs have enabled major advances in mechanized experimentation and closed-loop optimization, their scientific utility remains limited when tasks require literature-grounded reasoning, adaptive coordination, and interpretation beyond predefined search spaces. In this perspective, we examine how LLM-based agents may help bridge this gap by translating scientific intent into machine-executable workflows.
